# `modernize-deprecated-io`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: modernize · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports known pre-`std.Io` reader, writer, and buffering adapters reached
through `std.io` or `std.Io`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

The I/O redesign moves interface and buffer ownership into explicit current
types; old adapters delay an otherwise mechanical release migration.

## When it fires

Also reports `std.Io.Reader.readAlloc`, deprecated in Zig 0.17 in favor of
`readAllocAll` and scheduled for removal after 0.17. This exact alias receives a
safe member-name fix when its reader type or value is proven, including
immutable import and type aliases, typed parameters, and `Reader.fixed` results.

Shape-changing migrations name the replacement but do not edit code
automatically.

Other standard-library namespaces, nested `std` members, and declared local
bindings that shadow `std` are skipped.

Reader migration checks also skip custom readers, unknown factories, member
projections, and mutable namespace or type aliases. The replacement is
documented in [Zig 0.17's reader
implementation](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/src/tag/0.17.0/lib/std/Io/Reader.zig).

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

const read = std.Io.Reader.readAlloc;
```
